Orthopedics · published research

Knee arthroplasty

One randomized trial reported reduced early swelling and longer walking distance but no significant pain or range-of-motion difference; other trials report different, modality-specific outcomes.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

One randomized trial reported reduced early swelling and longer walking distance but no significant pain or range-of-motion difference; other trials report different, modality-specific outcomes.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact Surgery > Knee arthroplasty category contains seven titles: four human clinical studies, two reviews, and one protocol. The human group includes three randomized trials and one single-arm pilot. No animal or in-vitro/ex-vivo study was identified.

Human and clinical evidence

A 30-person randomized trial used dual LED PBM after knee replacement. It reported reduced swelling measures and a greater distance on the two-minute walk test, but no significant between-group difference in pain or range of motion (Chia et al. 2025). A 45-person three-arm trial compared low-level laser, broad-spectrum polarized light, and control conditions. Range of motion favored active treatment at some follow-ups but not at 12 months, with selected pain or analgesic outcomes also reported (Bahrami et al. 2022). Another randomized trial used laser acupuncture at 808 nm and reported reduced pain and morphine use during the first 72 hours (Huang et al. 2022). Acupuncture-point delivery is not the same intervention as localized PBM.

Animal evidence

No relevant animal study was identified in the exact arthroplasty category.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone cell or tissue experiment was listed for this indication.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The Chia trial used pulsed red and near-infrared LED light at 650 and 850 nm, 100–1000 Hz, reported irradiances of 8.4 and 13.5 mW/cm², and 1800 seconds per day for five days. The Bahrami trial compared an 804-nm laser at 500 mW and broad polarized light from 480 to 3400 nm at 40 mW/cm², with three treatment days. The Huang trial used 808-nm laser acupuncture at six points. These schedules and routes differ too much to define one general post-arthroplasty protocol.

Interpretation

Some short-term mobility or swelling outcomes improve in individual studies, but results vary and do not establish consistent pain relief or durable functional benefit.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow for early swelling or walking outcomes after selected knee-arthroplasty PBM protocols Very low for consistent pain relief or long-term functional benefit
Publications and records7 unique titles in exact Surgery > Knee arthroplasty category

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Four human publications include three randomized trials and one single-arm pilot, but they test different devices and outcomes. One reports early swelling and walking gains without pain or range-of-motion differences, and another uses laser acupuncture. More independent trials separating PBM from acupuncture and standard rehabilitation would clarify the effect.
